??? quote "Dialogue"

    - There is a verse in the oldest part of the long songs, among the chieftains of the Age of Division. A short one, seldom sung. A season before the Burning, it says, when the plateau beasts grew wild: goats that bit, cats that hunted people, birds that would not settle.
    - I have sung it alone every night this summer, and every night I hear Yarrek's goats in it, and the gnawers on the bridge. I do not trust my own ears any more. Would you ask [Odda](../npcs/odda_brenna.md) and [Thrun](../npcs/thrun_brenna.md) what they remember of it? Odda has heard me ask. You she may answer.
    - Ask them what they remember, not what they think. Memory first. Thinking is for afterwards.
    - Then I sing it alone again tonight. Perhaps the hundredth time will tell me.
    - Ask [Odda](../npcs/odda_brenna.md) and [Thrun](../npcs/thrun_brenna.md) what they remember of the beast verse.
    - So. Odda remembers old Hadda singing it, once, at a winter feast, and the hall going quiet. Thrun remembers its beat, slow and uneven, and remembers it under his hands this summer without meaning to.
    - That is not an answer. It is two people who heard what I heard. That is worth more to me than an answer. Thank you, *Player*. Whether I sing it at the gathering is still mine to decide.
    - Ahvi sent you about the verse. Of course. I have been asked, and I have not answered, and Ahvi is too kind to ask a third time.
    - I remember old Hadda singing it once, at a winter feast when I was a girl. The hall went quiet and the children stopped fidgeting. I never heard it sung in the hall again. Tell Ahvi that. Only that, for now.
    - The beast verse! Slow, uneven, a beat that limps. I have drummed it maybe twice in my life. Here, listen: dum, dum... dum. Like something that does not trust the ground.
    - Funny thing. This summer I caught my hands playing it on the table at supper, and I had not thought of it in years. Odda gave me a look. Tell Ahvi my hands remember it, even if I would rather they did not.
